title: India Extension
description: Indian succession — multi-personal-law system covering Hindu (coparcenary, HUF), Muslim personal law (school-based heir shares), Christian, Parsi, and Goa civil code estates; includes succession certificates and property classification

personalLaw.description: Which personal law governs this estate — India applies different succession laws based on religion

state.description: Indian state — different states have variations (e.g. agricultural land ceiling, stamp duty)

probateRequired.description: Whether probate is required — varies by religion and state. Mandatory for wills under Indian Succession Act in certain cities.

probateJurisdiction.description: Which court has jurisdiction — District Court or High Court depending on estate value

agriculturalLand.description: Agricultural land has special succession rules — cannot be willed in some states, subject to ceiling limits

willingRestriction.description: Whether agricultural land can be disposed of by will in this state

nriComplications.description: Non-Resident Indian complications — FEMA restrictions, repatriation limits, tax treaty implications

femaRestrictions.description: Whether FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act) restrictions apply

goaException.description: Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code — community of property regime applies regardless of religion

communityOfProperty.description: Whether community of property regime applies

stampDuty.description: Stamp duty on succession — varies by state

coparcenaryDetails.description: Hindu Succession Act coparcenary property rules — Mitakshara (most of India) vs Dayabhaga (Bengal)
coparcenaryDetails.$comment: This section overlaps with the hindu-succession extension which models coparcenary in greater detail. For Hindu estates, prefer the hindu-succession extension's HUFDetails and Coparcener definitions. This section is retained for backwards compatibility.

amendment2005Applies.description: Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act 2005 — daughters equal coparceners

propertyClassification.description: Ancestral vs self-acquired property distinction — ancestral property subject to coparcenary rules, self-acquired freely disposable

successionCertificate.description: Procedural mechanism for succession under Indian Succession Act ss.370-390

hufImplications.description: Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) implications — karta's interest passes by survivorship to coparceners

hufPropertyExcluded.description: HUF property passes by survivorship, not succession

muslimSuccessionRules.description: India-specific Muslim personal law application — school determines heir shares and distant kindred treatment

testamentaryThird.description: Can only bequeath 1/3 without heir consent

parsiSuccessionRules.description: Parsi succession rules under the Indian Succession Act 1925 Part V. Daughters receive half a son's share; widow receives equal to one child's share

daughterShareRule.description: Daughter's share relative to son — always half under Parsi law

widowShareRule.description: Widow's share — equal to one child's share

christianSuccessionRules.description: Christian succession under the Indian Succession Act 1925. Follows the ISA intestacy hierarchy with some state-specific deviations

followsIndianSuccessionAct.description: Whether succession follows the Indian Succession Act 1925 (true for most states)
